title: Tensor exactness and kernel flatness for a flat-quotient sheaf sequence
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $0\to F\to G\to H\to0$ be a short exact sequence of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], meaning a monomorphism followed by an epimorphism with image equal to kernel. Suppose $H$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $N$, the sequence $0\to F\otimes_{\mathcal O}N\to G\otimes_{\mathcal O}N\to H\otimes_{\mathcal O}N\to0$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is short exact. If $G$ is also flat, then $F$ is flat.

proof.text: Install the existing SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory, symmetricCategory and monoidalClosed structures. Mathlib MonoidalClosed makes tensorLeft a left adjoint, so it preserves finite colimits; BraidedCategory.tensorLeftIsoTensorRight transports this to tensorRight. The additive instances come from the existing MonoidalFree module. Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_epi now gives right exactness in both variables. The definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] gives finite-limit preservation for tensorRight of a flat object; the same braiding transports it to tensorLeft. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover] to N, obtaining an epic map P -> N with P flat, and form its kernelSequence T. It is short exact in the abelian category of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03EX (2), proof: choose a flat cover and its kernel

proof.text: The tensor rows S tensor Q, S tensor P and S tensor N are linked by mapNatTrans of curriedTensor.flip applied to the two maps of T. The top row is right exact, the middle-row first map is mono because P is flat, the right vertical map from the top to the middle is mono because S.X3 is flat, the left vertical map from the middle to the bottom is epi, and the middle column is exact. The private proved helper mono_bottom_of_tensor_rows performs the chase using Mathlib surjective_up_to_refinements_of_epi and ShortComplex.Exact.exact_up_to_refinements: lift x along the left epi to a, then lift its image along the middle column to b. Its image in the top-right object vanishes by cancellation of the right vertical mono. Lift b along the top row to c. Cancellation of the middle-row mono gives pi3 >> pi2 >> a = c >> phi.tau1. Composing with the left map to the bottom kills c, so the epic refinements pi1, pi2 and pi3 cancel to give x = 0. Together with right exactness this constructs ShortExact of S tensor N for every N. No points or sectionwise surjectivity are used.

source.place: Tag 03EX (2), the displayed tensor diagram and snake-lemma chase

proof.text: Assume S.X2 is also flat. For any mono f : U -> V, the composite (S.f tensor U) >> (S.X2 tensor f) is mono: the first map follows from the previous step and the second from flatness of S.X2. The whisker_exchange identity factors this composite through S.X1 tensor f; mono_of_mono_fac therefore makes that map mono. TensorLeft S.X1 preserves monomorphisms. Apply Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_mono, using right exactness and preservation of the first mono of every short exact sequence, to obtain finite-limit preservation. Transport this by the braiding to tensorRight S.X1, and combine with its finite-colimit preservation to obtain IsFlat S.X1.
